title: Singleton mass under the uniform law on a finite set
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let the uniform probability law on the $n$-element set $\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$ (the finite type $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$) assign equal mass to each point. Then for every element $i$, the mass of the singleton $\{i\}$ equals $\dfrac{1}{n}$.
hypotheses_covered: the measure is the uniform law on the n-element set Fin n
i is an element of Fin n
replaced: Each coordinate has mass $1 / n$ under the uniform law on \texttt{Fin n}.
